name: Beauvais-Tillé airport
before:
Branded Paris-Beauvais, and that name does a lot of work. The airport is 69 km north north west of the city, in Hauts-de-France rather than the Paris region, so a client booking what looks like a Paris flight needs to be told about the transfer before they book rather than after.

What it is good at is cheap seats. It is used mainly by low cost and charter airlines and handled just under four million passengers in 2016, which made it the tenth busiest airport in France.

The approach is better equipped than the terminal suggests. Runway 12 has a CAT III instrument landing system allowing landings in visibility down to 75 metres, which matters in a part of France that gets real winter fog.

It grew from a single 1979 hangar after Ryanair started flying to Dublin in 1997. A second terminal followed in 2010 and a new control tower in 2019.
after:
Branded Paris-Beauvais, and that name does a lot of work. The airport is 69 km north north west of Paris, in Hauts-de-France rather than the Paris region, so a client booking what looks like a Paris flight needs to be told about the transfer before they book rather than after.

What it is good at is cheap seats. The French airports' association says low-cost airlines carried more than 99 per cent of its traffic in 2025, when it handled about 6.7 million passengers and ranked ninth in France.

Its approach is better equipped than the terminal suggests. It has a Category III instrument landing system for very low visibility, which matters in a part of France that gets real winter fog.

The airport grew from a single terminal building of 1979 after Ryanair started flying to Dublin in 1997. A second terminal followed, and a new control tower in 2019.

claims.note: Coordinates: 69.0 km from the GeoNames centre of Paris at 346 degrees, north north west. 'Of the city' became 'of Paris' for clarity. GeoNames puts Beauvais in the Hauts-de-France region.

claims.claim: more than 99 per cent low cost in 2025; about 6.7 million passengers; ninth in France
claims.inAfter: The French airports' association says low-cost airlines carried more than 99 per cent of its traffic in 2025, when it handled about 6.7 million passengers and ranked ninth in France.
claims.note: Was 'It is used mainly by low cost and charter airlines and handled just under four million passengers in 2016, which made it the tenth busiest airport in France'. A passenger total replaces a passenger total. UAF, the French airports' association, gives 6,677,608 for 2025, ninth in metropolitan France, and more than 99 per cent low cost; Eurostat gives 6,675,611. Eurostat's own order puts it eighth only because it books most of Basel-Mulhouse's traffic to Switzerland, so the rank is attributed to UAF.
